titles.118: §.VIII: Dorscheans with Museus — Philippica mostly useful, yet Art. X said corrupted for Calvinists; first vs later wording
titles.119: §.VIII: Reply — honor the Philippica; later intra-Lutheran fights were not substance-changes; Art. X twin shift neither substantial nor more Calvinist
titles.120: §.VIII PRIUS: Invariata 1531 vs Variata Art. X — "exhibeantur" presupposes and says more than "adsint & distribuantur"
titles.121: §.VIII: Omitting "improbant secus docentes" is tautology-avoidance; German prototype sub specie; like omissions already in Invariata witnesses

titles.123: §.VIII close: Same spiritual reading fits the Invariata; its confessors allow spiritual presence; Reformed teach sacramental, not bare spiritual or corporal

latin.118:
§. VIII.
Equidem videri hic possum Dorschaanis, etiam modestioribus, Principium petere, cum Joh. Museo, Confess. Philippicam ita comparatam pronunciaturis, ut plerique quidem Articuli inibi fusius deducti & uberius declarati sint, multaque etiam utilia in ista Editione reperiantur; interim, ut quaedam etiam inserta fuerint, quae postea in controversiam vocarunt Augustanae Confessionis Theologi inter se, v. g. An Evangelium sit concio poenitentiae? Cumprimis verò, ut Articulus decimus de Coena Domini in gratiam Calvinianorum depravatus fuerit. Nam in Articulo X. primae Editionis haec haberi verba: De Coena Domini docent, quod Caro & Sanguis Christi verè adsit & distribuatur vescentibus, & improbant secus docentes. In altera verò Editione verba (Verè adsunt & distribuuntur) omissa esse, substitui autem haec: Quòd Corpus & Sanguis verè exhibentur &c. At verò formulam hanc loquendi, etiam concessisse Calvinianos; sed dixisse, quod spiritualiter exhibeantur. Deinde verba: Et improbant secus docentes, in Editione Philippica omissa esse, Atque hinc Controversiam de auctoritate hujus Confessionis ortam fuisse, Hactenus Museus Praelect. in Epitom. Formul. Concord. p. m. 32.
latin.119: Quibus Dorschaeanis modestioribus & Museanis respondemus (1.) Accipiendo quae de Confessione Philippi honorificè satis edisserunt, quaeque omnino urgent, non odiose eam exagitandam esse. (2.) advertendo, Confessioni Philippicae inserta ea, quae postea in controversiam vocarunt Aug. Conf. Theologi inter se (v. g. Num Evangelium sit Concio poenitentiae &c.) non talia fuisse, quae in Substantiam Veritatis, Articulis Augustanae Confessionis expositae, mutationem aliquam intulerunt, alioquin non talia fuissent, quae Augustanae Confess. Theologi, se inter, in controversiam vocassent. (3.) Contestando, articuli Xmi Mutationem duplicem, quae oppugnantibus eam maxima in oculis sudes est, (quasi in gratiam Calvinianorum facta, quae explodendae Pontificiae Transubstantiationi instituta unicè fuerat) nec Mutationem Substantialem inferre, nec Calvinianae, quam ajunt, Sententiae ulla ex parte magis favere, quam ipse Articulus X. invariatus ei favet.
latin.120: PRIUS patet ex verbis Articuli Xmi utriusque Confessionis inter se collatis, quae in Variata Anni 1531., communiter Invariata dicta, ita se habent: De Coena Domini docent, quod Corpus & Sanguis Christi verè adsint & distribuantur vescentibus in Coena Domini, & improbant secus docentes; In Variata autem vulgò dicta, sic sonant: De Coena Domini docent, quod Corpus & Sanguis Christi verè exhibeantur vescentibus in Coena Domini. Ubi meritò ad cujusvis Sensum & Intellectum provoco: Num duae dictae propositiones substantialiter inter se differant, praesertim quando posterior non tantum priorem supponit: (Corpus enim & Sanguis Christi dicta verè exhiberi in Coena, eô ipsô necesse est dici verè in Coena adesse & distribui); sed & posterior priori plus dicit: Nam adesse in Coena Corpus & Sanguis Christi verè possunt, nec non a ministro verè distribui, ut tamen non verè, communicantibus, certè non omnibus, exhibeantur; at, quandocunque in S. Coena à Ministro Corpus & Sanguis Christi communicantibus, verè exhibentur, necesse est & ea adesse, & ea distribui.
latin.121: Ad mutationem verò alteram quod attinet, seu potius omissionem Verborum horum in Variata: Et improbant secus docentes, etsi verba sic expressa inibi haud legi fateamur, in Confessionis tamen cujuscunque Articulis singulis subintelligi vel eadem, vel similia, videri necessariò debent: Qui enim positivè aliquid in Confessione fatetur, ille id semper, quod secus se habet, diffitetur ac improbat; Ut proinde omissio verborum istorum, Tautologiae duntaxat evitatio habenda sit, certè Substantialem mutationem nullam inducere queat. Taceo, quod ad priorem mutationem attinet, in prototypo Exemplari Invariatae Confessionis (prout id Germanica disertè ostendit) Articulum ita fuisse expressum, (non diffitente Dorscheo, cit. pag. 183.) De Coena Domini &c. fatentur, Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, sub specie panis & Vini, verè adesse; id quod Transubstantiationem Pontificiam per se, istô praesertim tempore, redoluisse, nulli facilè dubium esse potest. Unde etiam à Pontificiis Articulus hic, dictis verbis constans, simpliciter admissus fertur ab Historiographis Augustanae Confessionis omnibus. Quod ad posteriorem verò mutationem attinet, ignotum esse haud potest, & similem, imò prolixiorem multò improbationem omissam deprehendi in Augustanae Confessionis invariatae Exemplaribus Chytraei & Caelestini, inter se collatis, quoad Articulum XIII. & XVIII. (Quae tamen Omissio nihil prohibuit, quò minus ab Invariatae Confessionis Theologis utrumque Exemplar pro genuino habitum semper sit, hodièque habeatur.) & in plurimis Articulis e.g. in 3. 4. 6. 7. 11. 14. 18. 19. 20. 21. ne a prima quidem Aug. Confessionis adornatione improbationem contrariorum adjectam, nihilominus subaudiendam fuisse.
latin.122: POSTERIUS verò à nobis probandum, scil. mutationem praesertim priorem, Calvinianae Sententiae nullâ ex parte magis favere, quam ipse Articulus invariatus ei favet, sic illucescit: Quia cumprimis Calvinus, Reformatorum Doctoribus annumeratus, & cum Calvino Reformatae Ecclesiae omnes, & veram praesentiam, & veram distributionem Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, in S. Coena admittunt, non minùs quam veram exhibitionem, istasque propter hanc, quam nusquam non inculcant seriò, Signa Sacramentalia, non nude Significantia, sed & Exhibentia, confessi. Justas: At, sub Variatae Confessionis verbis, quibus Corpus & Sanguis Christi, nudè exhiberi, non autem adesse & distribui dicuntur, occultare facilius Calvinianos sententiam suam de Spirituali Corporis & Sanguinis Christi exhibitione posse, ut dum exhiberi ista dicunt verè, Spiritualiter duntaxat exhiberi doceant?
latin.123: Resp. (1.) Idem facere posse Calvinianos in verbis Invariatae Confessionis, ut dum dicunt: Corpus & Sanguinem Christi verè adesse & distribui, illa spiritualiter tantum adesse & distribui intelligant. (2.) Etiam invariatae solius Confessores, Spiritualem praesentiam pariter atque distributionem, haud magis quàm Exhibitionem ac Manducationem Spiritualem, inficiari, praesertim cum & suam Corporalem praesentiam, Distributionem, Manducationem & Exhibitionem, hyperphysicas nihilominus & Supernaturales inculcent esse. (3.) Non nudam Spiritualem praesentiam, Distributionem & Exhibitionem Corporis & Sanguinis Christi docere Reformatos, sed & Sacramentalem, licèt non Corporalem, utpote in neutra Confessione Augustana, nec in priori magis, quàm posteriori, edoctam.

pass_a.118: §. VIII. I may indeed seem here to the Dorscheans, even the more modest ones, to beg the principle, together with Johann Museus, who will pronounce the Philippica Confession so compared that most of the Articles in it are indeed drawn out more fully and declared more richly, and that many useful things are also found in that Edition; meanwhile, that some things have also been inserted which afterward the Theologians of the Augsburg Confession called into controversy among themselves, for example Whether the Gospel is a sermon of repentance? And especially, that the tenth Article on the Lord's Supper was corrupted in favor of the Calvinists. For in Article X of the first Edition these words are held: Concerning the Lord's Supper they teach that the Flesh and Blood of Christ are truly present and are distributed to those who eat, and they reject those who teach otherwise. But in the other Edition the words Truly are present and are distributed are said to have been omitted, and these substituted: That the Body and Blood are truly exhibited, and so on. But that the Calvinists also conceded this formula of speaking; yet said that they are exhibited spiritually. Then that the words And they reject those who teach otherwise were omitted in the Philippica Edition, and that from this the Controversy concerning the authority of this Confession arose. Thus far Museus, Lectures on the Epitome of the Formula of Concord, page 32.
pass_a.119: To which more modest Dorscheans and Museans we reply first by accepting what they have spoken honorably enough concerning Philip's Confession, and what altogether urge that it is not to be odiously harassed. Second by noting that those things inserted into the Philippica Confession which afterward the Augsburg-Confession Theologians called into controversy among themselves for example Whether the Gospel is a Sermon of repentance were not such as introduced any change into the Substance of Truth set forth in the Articles of the Augsburg Confession; otherwise they would not have been such as the Augsburg-Confession Theologians called into controversy among themselves. Third by contending that the twofold Mutation of Article X, which is the chief sweat in the eyes of those who attack it as if made in favor of the Calvinists though that Article had been instituted solely for exploding Pontifical Transubstantiation neither introduces a Substantial Mutation, nor favors in any part the Calvinian Sense as they call it more than the unvaried Article X itself favors it.
pass_a.120: The FORMER point is clear from the words of Article X of either Confession compared with each other, which in the Variata of the Year 1531, commonly called the Invariata, stand thus: Concerning the Lord's Supper they teach that the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present and are distributed to those who eat in the Lord's Supper, and they reject those who teach otherwise; but in the Variata commonly so called they sound thus: Concerning the Lord's Supper they teach that the Body and Blood of Christ are truly exhibited to those who eat in the Lord's Supper. Where I justly appeal to anyones Sense and Understanding: whether the two said propositions differ substantially from each other, especially when the latter not only presupposes the former for for the Body and Blood of Christ to be said to be truly exhibited in the Supper by that very fact it is necessary that they be said to be truly present in the Supper and distributed but the latter also says more than the former: For the Body and Blood of Christ can truly be present in the Supper and also be truly distributed by the minister and yet not truly be exhibited to the communicants certainly not to all; but whenever in the Holy Supper the Body and Blood of Christ are truly exhibited by the Minister to the communicants it is necessary both that they be present and that they be distributed.
pass_a.121: But as to the other mutation or rather the omission of these Words in the Variata And they reject those who teach otherwise although we confess that words so expressed are not read there yet in the several Articles of any Confession whatsoever the same or similar words must necessarily be understood as implied: For he who positively confesses something in a Confession always denies and rejects that which stands otherwise; so that the omission of those words is to be held merely as an avoidance of Tautology and certainly can introduce no Substantial mutation. I pass over as to the prior mutation that in the prototype Exemplar of the Invariata Confession as the German distinctly shows the Article was expressed thus Dorsche not denying it cited page 183: Concerning the Lord's Supper etc. they confess that the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present under the species of bread and Wine; which of itself especially at that time could easily be doubted by no one to have smelled of Pontifical Transubstantiation. Whence also this Article consisting of those words is reported by all the Historiographers of the Augsburg Confession to have been simply admitted by the Pontificals. But as to the latter mutation it cannot be unknown that a similar indeed much more prolix rejection is found omitted in the Invariata exemplars of the Augsburg Confession in Chytraeus and Caelestinus compared with each other as to Article XIII and XVIII which Omission nevertheless did not prevent either Exemplar from always being held and still today being held as genuine by the Theologians of the Invariata Confession; and that in very many Articles for example in 3 4 6 7 11 14 18 19 20 21 from the very first framing of the Augsburg Confession no rejection of contrary teachings was added and yet it was nevertheless to be understood as implied.
pass_a.122: But the LATTER point to be proved by us namely that the mutation especially the prior one favors the Calvinian Sense in no part more than the unvaried Article itself favors it becomes clear thus: Because first of all Calvin numbered among the Doctors of the Reformed and with Calvin all the Reformed Churches admit both a true presence and a true distribution of the Body and Blood of Christ in the Holy Supper no less than a true exhibition and on account of this exhibition which they nowhere fail to press seriously they have confessed the Sacramental Signs to be not nakedly Signifying but also Exhibiting. Fair enough: But the charge is that under the words of the Variata Confession by which the Body and Blood of Christ are said nakedly to be exhibited not however to be present and distributed the Calvinists can more easily hide their sense concerning the Spiritual exhibition of the Body and Blood of Christ so that while they say these are truly exhibited they teach that they are exhibited only Spiritually?
pass_a.123: Reply. First the Calvinists can do the same in the words of the Invariata Confession so that while they say the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present and distributed they understand them to be present and distributed only spiritually. Second even the confessors of the Invariata alone do not deny Spiritual presence equally with distribution any more than Spiritual Exhibition and Manducation especially since they also press that their own Corporal presence Distribution Manducation and Exhibition are nonetheless hyperphysical and Supernatural. Third the Reformed do not teach a naked Spiritual presence Distribution and Exhibition of the Body and Blood of Christ but also a Sacramental one though not a Corporal one inasmuch as a Corporal one is taught in neither Augsburg Confession nor in the earlier more than in the later.

118: §. VIII. Here I may seem, even to the more modest Dorscheans, to beg the question — standing with Johann Museus, who will weigh the Philippica Confession like this:
Most of its articles, they grant, are drawn out more fully and declared more richly, and many useful things appear in that edition.
Yet some insertions later set Augsburg-Confession theologians quarreling among themselves — for example, whether the Gospel is a sermon of repentance.
Above all, they say, Article X on the Lord's Supper was corrupted to favor the Calvinists.

In Article X of the first edition the words run: Concerning the Lord's Supper they teach that the flesh and blood of Christ are truly present and are distributed to those who eat, and they reject those who teach otherwise.
In the other edition, Museus reports, the words are truly present and are distributed drop out, and this is put in their place: that the body and blood are truly exhibited, and so on.
The Calvinists, he adds, even conceded that formula of speech — yet said the exhibition is spiritual.
Then the clause And they reject those who teach otherwise is omitted in the Philippica edition; and from that, he says, the controversy over this Confession's authority arose.
So far Museus, Lectures on the Epitome of the Formula of Concord, page 32.
119: To those more modest Dorscheans and Museans we answer:
First, we take what they have said honorably enough of Philip's Confession — and what presses hardest of all: it is not to be odiously harassed.

Second, the insertions later fought over among Augsburg-Confession theologians for example whether the Gospel is a sermon of repentance did not change the substance of the truth set out in the Augsburg articles. Had they done so, those same theologians would not have been fighting the points among themselves.

Third, we contend that Article X's twin mutation — the chief sweat in the attackers' eyes, as if Melanchthon had altered it for the Calvinists, though the article was framed solely to explode pontifical transubstantiation — neither introduces a substantial change, nor favors the so-called Calvinian sense in any part more than the unvaried Article X itself already does.
120: The first point is plain once you set the two forms of Article X side by side.

In the 1531 Variata — commonly called the Invariata — it runs: Concerning the Lord's Supper they teach that the body and blood of Christ are truly present and are distributed to those who eat in the Lord's Supper, and they reject those who teach otherwise.
In the Variata commonly so named it sounds: Concerning the Lord's Supper they teach that the body and blood of Christ are truly exhibited to those who eat in the Lord's Supper.
I appeal to anyone's sense: do these two propositions differ in substance?

The later wording not only presupposes the earlier — for if Christ's body and blood are truly exhibited in the Supper, then by that very fact they must be said to be truly present there and distributed — but also says more.
Body and blood can truly be present in the Supper, and truly distributed by the minister, and yet not truly exhibited to the communicants — certainly not to all.
But whenever in the holy Supper the minister truly exhibits Christ's body and blood to the communicants, they must both be present and be distributed.
121: As for the other change — or rather the omission in the Variata of And they reject those who teach otherwise — we admit those exact words are not read there.
Yet in every article of any confession the same sense, or something like it, must be understood: whoever positively confesses a point always denies and rejects what stands against it.
So the omission is only an avoidance of tautology; it can introduce no substantial mutation.

I pass over this further note on the prior change: in the prototype exemplar of the Invariata as the German plainly shows, and Dorsche does not deny it page 183, the article was expressed thus — Concerning the Lord's Supper they confess that the body and blood of Christ are truly present under the species of bread and wine — which at that time could easily smell of pontifical transubstantiation by itself.
Hence the historiographers of the Augsburg Confession report that the pontificals simply admitted this article in those words.

And as for the later omission, it is no secret that a similar — indeed much longer — rejection is missing in the Invariata exemplars of Chytraeus and Caelestinus when Article XIII and XVIII are compared; yet that omission never kept Invariata theologians from treating either exemplar as genuine then or now.
In many articles besides — 3, 4, 6, 7, 11, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21 — no rejection of contrary teaching was added even at the Confession's first framing, and yet it was still to be heard as implied.
122: The second point we must prove — that the change, especially the prior one, favors the Calvinian sense no more than the unvaried article itself does — comes clear this way.

Calvin, counted among the Reformed doctors, and with him all the Reformed churches, admit a true presence and a true distribution of Christ's body and blood in the holy Supper, no less than a true exhibition.
And because of that exhibition, which they never fail to press, they confess the sacramental signs to be not bare signs only, but also exhibiting signs.

Fair enough. But the charge runs: under the Variata's words, where body and blood are said only to be exhibited, not to be present and distributed, Calvinists can more easily hide a merely spiritual exhibition — saying truly exhibited while teaching exhibited only spiritually.
123: Answer. First, they can do the same with the Invariata's words: while it says Christ's body and blood are truly present and distributed, they may take that as only spiritual presence and distribution.

Second, even confessors of the Invariata alone do not deny spiritual presence and distribution any more than spiritual exhibition and eating — especially since they also insist that their own corporal presence, distribution, eating, and exhibition are nonetheless hyperphysical and supernatural.

Third, the Reformed do not teach a naked spiritual presence, distribution, and exhibition of Christ's body and blood, but a sacramental one as well — though not a corporal one, which neither Augsburg Confession teaches, earlier or later.
